newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL IMPORT FINANCING RULES HAVING EFFECT.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL IMPORT FINANCING RULES HAVING EFFECT.

text.p: Short-term import financing restrictions introduced by Brazil earlier this year have had a marked effect, officials said Monday.

Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, economic policy secretary at the Finance Ministry, said financing of over one year had increased 475 percent in January-July 1997 compared with the same period a year ago.
He said cash payments for imports fell 4.0 percent, financing of under six months rose 180 percent and financing of between six months and a year sunk 24 percent.
In a statement, the Finance Ministry noted that while one-year-and-above financing applied to just 3.14 percent of imports in January this year, it applied to 31.87 percent of imports last month.
In June, 22.39 percent of imports had financing of more than 360 days while in April the proportion stood at 8.65 percent.

Citing abuse of interest rate arbitrage opportunities, Brazil imposed new rules on March 26 which effectively forced importers to pay in cash or seek financing in excess of 360 days. The move provoked an outcry from Mercosur customs union partners Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, who were promptly given partial exemptions.
Other trading partners, in particular the United States, say they are also concerned the measures infringe the spirit of free trade.
